subject: history
title: Research Study Report (RSR)
keyDates: Autumn 2026 (TBC by SEC) — SEC circular and the digital RSR booklet for 2027 are expected; the 2026 equivalent circular (S57/25) went out in October 2025
Late 2026 to early 2027 — agree a topic and outline plan with your teacher before doing substantive work; the 2026 pattern had the booklet available once SEC published it (TBC by SEC for 2027)

Completion date 2027 — TBC by SEC. Previous completion dates: 26 April 2024 (SEC circular S75/23) and 17 April 2026 (SEC Schools Portal circular S57/25); a search snippet gave 4 April 2025 but I could not confirm it from the SEC document. Expect April; your school will set an earlier internal deadline

Shortly after completion date 2027 — teacher uploads your PDF through the SEC Schools Portal; the Schools Portal re-opens for a few days in May only for candidates granted an extension (2026 pattern; 2027 TBC)
June 2027 — the printed copy of the booklet stays in school until the appeals process ends; the written History exam is 80% of the grade
summary: The RSR is a booklet-based piece of coursework worth 100 marks (20% of your History grade) at both levels. You choose a narrow, historically significant subject with your teacher, then complete an outline plan, an evaluation of your sources and an extended essay that includes a review of the research process. It is written under teacher supervision, authenticated by your teacher and principal, and submitted to the SEC before the written exam.

stages.name: Choose and define your subject
stages.marksNote: No marks of its own, but the title drives every section (15 + 25 + 60 = 100 marks in total)

guide.h: What the syllabus requires of the subject
points: The subject must be of historical significance, chosen by you under the direction of your teacher.
It must be clearly defined and narrow rather than broad, so you can investigate it in depth. 'The Great Famine' is too broad; a single estate, workhouse or county during the Famine is the right size.
It must not be obscure or trivial, and it must rest on information that can be authenticated by an examiner.
Local history and historiographical studies (how historians have interpreted something) are both explicitly allowed by the syllabus.

The SEC has said it recommends choosing within your Field of Study (Early Modern or Later Modern), but material outside it is acceptable as long as it is historically significant. This comes from SEC advice for teachers dated about 2013, so confirm with your teacher.
The SEC will not award marks for historical content more recent than 1993 for Irish history or 1992 for Europe and the wider world. This is stated in the SEC circular S75/23.
Check the end of your topic as well as the start: a topic that begins in 1980 but runs into 1995 loses marks for the later material.
HIST (the History In-Service Team) advises putting a date or dates in your title; so does the Wicklow County Archives guide.

guide.h: Making sure the topic is workable
points: Before you commit, confirm you can get at least three suitable sources (two at Ordinary Level). A topic with thin source material will cap your evaluation and essay marks.
Pick something you already understand well enough to give historical context, especially at Higher Level (HIST advice).
Write your title so that it allows you to analyse evidence, weigh viewpoints and reach a conclusion, not just tell a story.

Wicklow County Archives suggests testing significance against four questions: was it remarkable, was it remembered, did it result in change, is it revealing. Meeting at least one helps you justify the subject in the outline plan.
Your teacher must be happy with the subject and the outline plan before you go further (HIST advice).

I could not find a published SEC rule on whether your RSR subject may overlap with the documents-based topic on the 2027 paper. Ask your teacher to check the current SEC circular and Guidelines for Teachers.

checklistCandidates: Pick a narrow subject with a clear title that includes dates
Keep every part of the subject on or before 1993 (Ireland) or 1992 (Europe/world)
Confirm at least three suitable sources exist before committing
Get your teacher's approval of the subject and plan

stages.name: Research and gather sources
stages.marksNote: Feeds the outline plan citations (6 marks), the evaluation (25) and the research-skills mark in the essay (15)

points: Sources must be primary or specialist secondary. 'Standard school textbooks will not be regarded as suitable sources' (DES/NCCA Guidelines, p.14, quoted in the 2025 SEC marking scheme).
Wicklow County Archives explains specialist secondary as focused on one topic or period; a general Junior Cycle History textbook is not specialist because it covers many topics in little depth.
Higher Level needs at least three sources; Ordinary Level at least two. Using more is allowed. Wicklow advises listing three in the outline plan and putting the rest in a bibliography at the end.
HIST advises that, where available, at least one source should be written by a historian.

Examples of primary sources named by Wicklow: newspapers, official documents, government reports, speeches, interviews, autobiographies, diaries, letters. Secondary: books, biographies, articles, most websites, documentaries, podcasts.
If you cite an oral-history interview, a transcript must be available for authentication (SEC advice for teachers, about 2013).

Log every source's details at the time you read it: author, title, publisher, place and year for books; author, page title, date written, URL and date accessed for websites. You need these for the outline plan and for footnotes.
Note strengths, weaknesses and bias while reading, not afterwards. You will forget by the time you write the evaluation.
File notes under the headings you plan to use as your aims and essay paragraphs. HIST suggests brainstorming these headings straight after choosing a title.
Take notes in your own words. Copying text invites plagiarism problems (see rules).
Check bibliographies and footnotes in your sources for leads to further sources.
Keep notes, drafts and any interview tapes or transcripts until the appeals process is finished (HIST advice).

guide.h: Use of AI and internet material
points: The SEC circular S75/23 says all research sources must be referenced, including material generated using AI software, and that suspected AI copying, improper assistance or procuring work is investigated as plagiarism.
Treat internet pages with care: HIST warns that some historical-looking sites are biased or propaganda. Ask your teacher if unsure whether a website is suitable.

checklistCandidates: Use at least 3 primary or specialist-secondary sources (2 at OL), no school textbooks
Include at least one source by a historian where available
Record full citation details for every source as you read it
Keep notes and drafts until appeals close

stages.name: Outline plan
stages.marksNote: 15 marks, same at Higher and Ordinary: 9 for define/justify, aims and approach (3 each) and 6 for citing sources

points: Define and justify your subject: say exactly what you will study and why it is historically significant and why you chose it (3 marks).

Identify your aims: what you want to find out about the subject (3 marks). Wicklow advises 3 to 5 aims, in the future tense (for example 'I intend to establish why...'), and about the subject itself, not about your skills.

Indicate your intended approach: how you will carry out the research (3 marks). Cover where you will look for sources, how you will choose and cross-check them, how you will store information and how you will use teacher feedback and redrafting.
Cite the sources you will consult (6 marks).

The outline plan goes on its own page in the booklet. The SEC says material for the outline plan and evaluation must be written on the appropriate pages and marks are not awarded for such material elsewhere in the booklet.

guide.h: Citing sources to earn the 6 marks
points: Each of three sources earns up to 2 marks: 1 mark for author plus title only, and 1 further mark for an extra piece of validating information such as publisher or date (SEC 2025 marking scheme).
For a written source the SEC circular asks for author's name, title of the book or article, publisher and date of publication.
For a website give enough accurate detail for an examiner to authenticate it: author, title of the page or article, date written if available, URL and the date you read or downloaded it.

At Ordinary Level Wicklow's guide describes two sources at 3 marks each; the SEC 2025 marking scheme I found only sets out the three-source version, so confirm the Ordinary Level split with your teacher.
In the outline plan you only list the sources. Commenting on them belongs in the evaluation section.
The three 3-mark elements (define and justify, aims, approach) are each graded very good = 3, good = 2, fair = 1 on how clearly and coherently you do them.
Wicklow says failing to explain historical significance is how many students lose marks here.

checklistCandidates: Define the subject and explain why it is historically significant
State 3 to 5 aims about the subject, in the future tense
Explain how you will research it, step by step
Cite 3 sources (2 at OL) with author, title and publisher or date
Write the outline plan on the outline plan page only

stages.name: Evaluation of sources
stages.marksNote: 25 marks, Higher and Ordinary. Marks depend on how many sources you evaluate: all three gets the top band

points: For each source, state what type it is and whether it is primary or secondary (Wicklow advice).
Indicate how relevant it is to your subject: how much of it was about your topic, what you got from it, whether it answered any of your aims.
Comment on strengths and on weaknesses. The syllabus wording is 'strengths and limitations'; the marking scheme says 'strengths and/or weaknesses', but do both for every source.
Compare sources: say which was most useful and why (Wicklow advice).
Be honest. Wicklow advises against calling a source useless; if you got nothing from it you should not have chosen it.
Refer to the sources briefly (for example Source 1, or the author's name) because space is limited.
Who produced it, and are they an eyewitness, a participant or a historian?
Is there bias, propaganda or an ulterior motive?
Does it give sources of its own (footnotes, bibliography) or just assertions?
Is it up to date, and does it include information the others lack?
Does it contradict other sources, and how would you check which is right?
Is it easy to use: contents page, glossary, maps, photographs, readable language?
For websites: who wrote it, when was it last updated, is it mostly opinion, can others edit it? (HIST advice)

guide.h: How the 25 marks are banded (Higher Level)
points: Reference to all three sources: excellent 22-25, very good 17-21, good 13-16, fair 9-12, weak 0-8.
Reference to only two sources: excellent 15-17 at most. Only one source: excellent 8-9 at most.
So evaluating fewer than three sources puts a hard ceiling on your mark however well you write.

The Ordinary Level bands in the Wicklow guide are shown for two sources (top band 21-25) and one source (top band 14-17); these are the SEC bands as reproduced by Wicklow, not read directly from an SEC document.
The section is on its own page(s) of the booklet. The SEC says content written elsewhere is not credited.

checklistCandidates: Evaluate every source you cited (all three at HL)
Say whether each source is primary or secondary
Give relevance, at least one strength and one weakness for each source
Compare the sources and say which helped most
Write only on the evaluation pages

stages.name: Extended essay
stages.marksNote: 50 of the 60 marks: historical knowledge 25, research skills 15, presentation 10 (the other 10 are for the review). Length: Higher 1,200 to 1,500 words; Ordinary 600 to 800 words

points: Historical knowledge (25): thorough, accurate and relevant to your title. Excellent is 21-25; weak is 0-5.
Research skills (15): appropriate depth of investigation, use of sources, and fair and balanced treatment of issues. Excellent is 13-15.
Presentation (10): literacy, coherence and structure. Excellent is 9-10.
The essay is marked as a unit out of 50.
The syllabus requires clear coherence: an introduction, a conclusion and a line of logical development between them.
Set out your main findings and conclusions, and answer the aims you gave in your outline plan.
Organise by the headings from your planning stage, one main idea per paragraph, with linking phrases between paragraphs.
Use facts, figures, statistics, quotations and the views of historians from your sources, and keep it all relevant to the title.
Footnote quotations (HIST and Wicklow both advise this): a small number beside the quote, with a matching note giving source type, name, author and page.
Use evidence from all your sources, not just the one you liked best.
Treat issues fairly: show different interpretations where they exist, then reach a judgement.
Avoid mere narrative. Tell the examiner what the evidence shows and why it matters.
Proofread for spelling, grammar and punctuation. The booklet is now completed digitally (see submission stage), so legibility is about layout rather than handwriting.

The SEC circular says these ranges are 'deemed appropriate' for the extended essay: Higher 1,200-1,500 and Ordinary 600-800 words. They are ranges, not stated penalty thresholds; I found no SEC statement of a specific marks penalty for going outside them, but stay inside.

Whether the review counts towards the word range is unclear: the Wicklow guide says it does (and gives review lengths of about 200-300 words at HL, 100-200 at OL), while the SEC circular and marking scheme refer to the essay length and do not say. See conflicts and ask your teacher.

checklistCandidates: Write an introduction, a logical middle and a conclusion
Answer the aims from your outline plan
Use accurate facts and evidence relevant to the title
Draw on all your sources and footnote quotations
Show fair, balanced treatment of the issues
Stay within 1,200-1,500 words (HL) or 600-800 (OL)

stages.name: Review of the research process, final checks and submission
stages.marksNote: 10 marks for the review, Higher and Ordinary. Bands: excellent 9-10, very good 7-8, good 5-6, fair 3-4, weak 0-2

points: The review can be part of the essay or a separate section, and examiners assess it in its totality (SEC 2025 marking scheme).
The syllabus says it should show how the research process was undertaken and how useful it was in achieving the aims in your outline plan.
Refer back to your outline plan aims and say, with reasons, whether you achieved each.
Be specific to your project. Wicklow warns against vague statements like 'I found sources'; say how you found them, where, and what difficulties came up.

Cover: how you chose the title, problems with sources or conflicting information, how you recorded information, drafts and teacher feedback, anything that surprised you, and what you would do differently.
Wicklow advises starting it on a new page with a heading.

From 2025 the SEC replaced paper reporting booklets with digital booklets for History, Geography and Religious Education (circular S75/23). Candidates convert the finished booklet to PDF, print the final PDF, check every page is visible, and the teacher uploads the PDF through the SEC Schools Portal (SEC circular S57/25 for 2026). Expect the same for 2027 unless SEC says otherwise; 2027 circular is TBC.
Any work not visible on the printed copy of the PDF cannot gain marks. When you sign the P.2 form you confirm the printed copy matches the uploaded one.
Complete only one booklet. Do not use the specimen booklet to submit work; work in a specimen is deemed invalid.
If you complete the RSR through Irish, use the Irish booklet; there are no bonus marks for coursework in Irish (circular S75/23).
Repeat candidates must submit new coursework not previously submitted.
Digital booklets are in Word format and may be completed in other software such as Google Docs, but must be converted to PDF; do not create fillable PDFs.
The booklet must be your own unaided work, completed under your teacher's supervision. Both your class teacher and your principal certify it (circular S75/23).
Copying, plagiarism (including AI use), improper assistance or procuring work are investigated by SEC personnel and can invalidate the work.

checklistCandidates: Write the review about your own project, referring to your outline plan aims
Say whether you achieved each aim and why
Describe real problems you met and what you would change
Check the whole booklet against the checklist and proofread
Convert to PDF, print it and confirm every page is visible
Sign the authentication form only when the work is entirely your own

criteria.name: Outline plan: define and justify the subject
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A clearly defined, narrow subject with a reasoned explanation of why it is historically significant and why you chose it (very good = 3).

criteria.name: Outline plan: aims
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Clear, focused aims about the subject itself, not about your skills (very good = 3).

criteria.name: Outline plan: intended approach
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A clear, practical account of how you will carry out the research (very good = 3).

criteria.name: Outline plan: citation of sources
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Three appropriate (non-textbook) sources, each with author, title and a further validating detail such as publisher or date (2 marks each at HL).

criteria.name: Evaluation of sources
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Clear, coherent comments on relevance, strengths and weaknesses of all three sources (HL) to reach the top band of 22-25.

criteria.name: Extended essay: historical knowledge
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Thorough, accurate content relevant to the title (excellent = 21-25).

criteria.name: Extended essay: research skills
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Appropriate depth of investigation, clear use of sources and fair, balanced treatment of issues (excellent = 13-15).

criteria.name: Review of the research process
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A specific, honest review of how the research went and how useful it was in achieving your outline-plan aims (excellent = 9-10).

rules: Marks are not awarded for historical content more recent than 1993 (Ireland) or 1992 (Europe and the wider world).
Sources must be primary or specialist secondary; standard school textbooks are not accepted as suitable sources.
Use at least three sources at Higher Level and at least two at Ordinary Level.
Outline plan and evaluation material must be written on their own pages of the booklet; marks are not awarded for such material elsewhere in the booklet.
Extended essay length: Higher 1,200 to 1,500 words, Ordinary 600 to 800 words.
Submit only one booklet; do not submit work done in a specimen booklet.
The work must be your own, done under teacher supervision, and certified by your teacher and your principal.
All sources must be referenced and acknowledged, including any AI-generated material; unreferenced copying counts as plagiarism.

Use blue or black pen for any paper elements, and avoid correction fluid and fluorescent markers; colour and pencil only for graphs, sketches and diagrams (SEC circular S75/23, written for the paper booklet).
Digital booklet: convert to PDF, print and check every page; work not visible on the printed copy gains no marks.
Repeat candidates must submit new coursework not previously submitted.
Keep notes, drafts and any oral-history transcripts until the appeals process has finished.
mistakes: Choosing a topic that is too broad to investigate in depth.
Choosing a topic or covering events that run past 1993 (Ireland) or 1992 (Europe/world), so those parts earn nothing.
Using a school textbook, or only general sources, instead of primary or specialist secondary sources.
Failing to explain why the subject is historically significant in the outline plan (Wicklow flags this as a common loss of marks).
Writing aims about your skills or process instead of about the subject.
Citing sources with author and title only, so you miss the extra mark for publisher or date.
Evaluating fewer than three sources (HL), which caps the evaluation mark.
Calling a source good or bad without saying why, or listing only strengths.
Writing the evaluation or outline plan material on the wrong page of the booklet.
Telling a story instead of answering the aims with evidence and a conclusion (mere narrative).
Ignoring some of your sources in the essay, or quoting without footnotes.
A generic review ('I found sources and wrote the essay') instead of one specific to your project and tied to your outline plan.
Leaving the work until close to the deadline; a teacher guide on Scoilnet advises finishing early and working steadily through the year.
Submitting a PDF where parts of the booklet are not visible on the printed copy.

conflicts: Word count and the review: the Wicklow guide says the review is included in the 1,200-1,500 / 600-800 word count (review about 200-300 words HL, 100-200 OL). SEC S75/23 and the 2025 marking scheme describe the range for the 'Extended Essay' (marked 60 = essay 50 + review 10) without saying whether the review counts. Ask your teacher; the safe approach is to keep essay plus review inside the range.

Page allocation: Wicklow says evaluation of sources has 2 pages in the booklet, while HIST (older, paper booklet) says the evaluation must be on one page. SEC only says content must be on the 'appropriate pages'. Use the layout of the 2027 booklet.
Ordinary Level outline-plan citations: Wicklow describes 2 sources x 3 marks; the SEC 2025 marking scheme only gives 3 sources x 2 marks. I could not find the Ordinary Level SEC scheme.

Submission method: older sources (PDST 2013, Wicklow) describe a handwritten paper booklet; SEC S75/23 and S57/25 say digital booklets, converted to PDF and uploaded by the school, from 2025. Pen colour rules apply to paper only.
Completion date: 26 April 2024 (S75/23), 17 April 2026 (S57/25) and an unconfirmed 4 April 2025. No 2027 date was found; mark as TBC by SEC.
Topic must not clash with the documents-based topic? Not found in any source I could read, so this is unknown, not 'no'.
Chief Examiner's report: I could not locate an SEC Chief Examiner's report for the History RSR, so common-mistake advice comes from teacher and archive guides rather than examiner reports.

New History specification: a draft was released for consultation in March 2026; it applies to later cohorts and not to students sitting in June 2027, but the RSR arrangements could be affected for later years.

App cross-check (exam-breakdown.js line 294): 'Your Research Study Report is a further 100 marks (20% of the grade) on top of this 400-mark paper'. Consistent with the SEC syllabus (20% RSR, 80% paper). No contradiction.
